reason: The text extensively depicts leaders (Moses and the elders) and the people collaborating throughout the covenant narrative (Exodus 19-24). Moses serves as a mediator between God and the people, calling the elders and presenting God's words to them. The people respond unanimously and collectively to the covenant proposals: 'all that the Lord has spoken, we will do' (כָּל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נַעֲשֶׂ֑ה). There is clear communication, coordination, and mutual agreement between leadership and people. However, this statement's applicability is significantly complicated by the golden calf narrative (Exodus 32), where the people pressure Aaron into creating an idol while Moses is absent on the mountain—demonstrating the opposite of leadership-people collaboration. The text thus presents both the ideal of collaborative leadership and the consequences when it breaks down.
